cache.representation: Original feed bytes base64-encoded with SHA-256 in one bundle; index validated/rebuilt in memory. Hashes are integrity checks, not publisher signatures.
cache.dependencies: Only standard-library imports added; no lock, SBOM or software license changes needed; public datasets not bundled

ci_run_after_push.failing_test: NetworkTests.test_real_tls_header_and_body_stalls_cancel_deadline_and_end_worker, all four header/cancel/deadline subtests; 611 tests, 77 skipped on Windows
ci_run_after_push.cause: Windows does not wake a cut-off TLS read, so the request worker ends at its socket timeout (budget + 1, about 1.25 seconds here); the test waited only 1 second. The existing Wazuh stalled-request tests already allow for this. Production downloads cannot reach this on Windows, where the cache backend fails closed before any request.
ci_run_after_push.fix: Test only: wait up to 3 seconds for the worker on Windows (1 second elsewhere) and assert on every OS that the caller is released within 1 second
ci_run_after_push.local_verification: macOS NetworkTests pass on Python 3.14.10 and 3.15.2. A synthetic loopback simulation with the cut-off disabled released the caller in 0.11-0.26 seconds and ended the worker 1.01-1.17 seconds later, reproducing the CI failure and fitting the new Windows wait. Windows itself is verified only by the next CI run.

ci_rerun_after_fix.windows_tests: Python 3.11, 3.14 and 3.15 each ran 611 tests: OK, 77 skipped on Windows; the stalled-download test passed in all three
ci_rerun_after_fix.other_jobs: macOS and Ubuntu tests and all npm launcher jobs, including Windows, succeeded
